references.text: Israel is convinced that Joseph is alive and decides to go see him before he dies.
Joseph meets his father Israel in Goshen, and they weep for a long time in each other's arms – the immediate context of Israel's words.
Simeon says he can now depart from here in peace after having seen the Lord's salvation – a strong parallel to Israel's words about being able to die after seeing Joseph's face.
Jacob's death declaration in 46:30 is directly linked to his prophetic blessing concerning God's future guidance in 48:21.
Both verses highlight Jacob's deep gratitude for getting to see Joseph (and his children) again, something he had not thought possible.
Joseph repeats his father's death declaration and prophecy (46:30) to confirm that God's promise of the land will survive through generations.
Joseph makes concrete his father Jacob's prophetic hope (46:30) by demanding that his bones be taken when God fulfills the promise of the land.
